statement: A paper heart has an up-and-down line of symmetry. Ana folds the heart along that line. The folded shape is 6 cm tall and 4 cm wide. How wide is the whole heart?

choices.misconception: I gave the width of the folded shape, but folding hid the other half of the heart.
I added the height and the width, 6 + 4.
I doubled the height instead of the width.
I multiplied the height by the width, 6 x 4.

hints: What does folding along the line do to the heart?
Folding along a line of symmetry puts one half exactly on top of the other. This fold line runs up and down, so the folded shape keeps the full height but shows only part of the width.
The folded shape is one half of the heart, so the whole heart is two of those halves side by side.

solutions.reliable: Folding along the up-and-down line puts the left half exactly on top of the right half. The height stays 6 cm, but the folded shape is only half as wide as the heart. The whole heart is two halves side by side: 4 + 4 = 8 cm wide. The idea to keep: a line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves, so unfolding doubles the size across the fold.

whyOnTest: Line symmetry: the fold line splits the heart into two matching halves, so unfolding doubles the width but not the height.
